    AI Overview
    A bell is a hollow, typically metal percussion instrument (idiophone) that produces a ringing sound when struck by an internal clapper or external hammer. Used globally for signaling, music, or warnings in churches, schools, and ships, they range from small handbells to large towers. Common types include cups, gongs, and jingle bells. 
    Key Associations: 
    • Bell Textron: A major aerospace manufacturer known for helicopters and vertical lift aircraft.
    • Bell Helmets: A renowned brand specializing in helmets for motorsports and cycling safety.
    • Bell Canada: A large Canadian telecommunications company.
    • Symbolism: Often signifies warnings, timekeeping, or beginnings/endings.
    • Meaning: Originates from English, often meaning "beautiful".

    Dictionary
    Definitions from Oxford Languages · Learn more
    bell1
    /bel/
    Learn to pronounce
    noun
    noun: bell; plural noun: bells
    1. 1.
      a hollow object, typically made of metal and having the shape of a deep inverted cup widening at the lip, that sounds a clear musical note when struck, typically by means of a clapper inside.
      "the church bells tolled"
      h
      Similar:
      chime
      gong
      alarm
      peal
      knell
      toll
      signal
      warning
      alert
      tocsin
      • a device that includes or sounds like a bell, used to give a signal or warning.
        "a bicycle bell"
      • a bell rung to denote intervals of time, such as (in boxing and other sports) to mark the start or end of a round.
        noun: the bell
        "at the bell, we dashed out of Latin class"
    2. 2.
      a bell-shaped object or part of something.
      • the end of a trumpet or other brass instrument.
        "the acoustic properties of a trumpet's bell"
      • Botany
        the corolla of a bell-shaped flower.
        "a flower with small pale blue bells"
      • Zoology
        the umbrella of a jellyfish.
        "the tiny jellyfish has a bell measuring five to ten millimeters wide"
    3. 3.
      a musical instrument consisting of a set of cylindrical metal tubes of different lengths, suspended in a frame and played by being struck with a hammer.
    4. 4.
      Nautical
      (preceded by a numeral) the time as indicated every half hour of a watch by the striking of the ship's bell one to eight times.
      "at five bells in the forenoon of June 11"
    verb
    verb: bell; 3rd person present: bells; past tense: belled; past participle: belled; gerund or present participle: belling
    1. 1.
      provide with a bell or bells; attach a bell or bells to.
      "the young men were belling and hobbling the horses before releasing them"
    2. 2.
      make a ringing sound likened to that of a bell.
      "the organ belling away"
    3. 3.
      spread or flare outward like the lip of a bell.
      "her shirt belled out behind"
    Phrases
    bell the cat
    take the danger of a shared enterprise upon oneself.
    bells and whistles
    attractive additional features or trimmings. "an advocate of more bells and whistles on the income tax code"
    be saved by the bell
    (in boxing and other sports) be saved from being counted out by the ringing of the bell at the end of a round.
    as clear as a bell
    (of sound) perfectly clear. "Aunt Nora's words came clear as a bell"
    ring a bell
    revive a distant recollection; sound familiar. "the name Woodall rings a bell"
    with bells on
    enthusiastically. "everybody's waiting for you with bells on"
    Origin
    Old English belle, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch bel, and perhaps to bell2.
    bell2
    /bel/
    Learn to pronounce
    noun
    noun: bell; plural noun: bells
    1. the cry of a stag or buck at rutting time.
    verb
    verb: bell; 3rd person present: bells; past tense: belled; past participle: belled; gerund or present participle: belling
    1. (of a stag or buck) make a cry at rutting time.
    Origin
    Old English bellan ‘to bellow’, of Germanic origin; related to German bellen ‘to bark, bray’, and perhaps also to bell1.
    Tip
    Similar-sounding words
    bell is sometimes confused with bel
    Use over time for: bell
